events.title: The battle of the Frigidus
events.shortBlurb: On the river Frigidus Theodosius broke the army of the usurper Eugenius, and with it the last armed hope of Roman paganism…
body: When Valentinian II died at Vienne in 392, the Frankish general Arbogast raised to the western throne his secretary Eugenius, a teacher of rhetoric, and with him the pagan party of the senate made its last restoration: the Altar of Victory returned to the curia, and the old gods rode once more with the standards.

Theodosius I marched from the East and met them in the Julian Alps, on the river Frigidus — the Vipava of our maps — on 5 and 6 September 394. The first day cost him dear, his Gothic vanguard falling in thousands; but on the second, the church historians relate, the Bora wind rose and blew into the faces of the westerners, turning their own missiles back upon them.

Eugenius was taken in his tent and beheaded; Arbogast fled to the mountains and two days later fell upon his sword. Theodosius, master now of a world momentarily undivided, died at Milan the following January, leaving the empire to his sons Arcadius and Honorius — and the Frigidus has stood ever since as the last battle fought in the names of the old gods.
